gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify the false claim that every vertically closed (p-1,2)-form on the prolongation space has the special nearest-neighbour mixed-shift form. ISSUE-001 explicitly recognises arbitrary prolongation-coordinate differentials and gives a counterexample, matching the gold defect and repair.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The asserted automatic reduction of arbitrary vertically closed forms to the specific nearest-neighbour shifted/unshifted representation is false; general forms may use arbitrary finite shift indices, so the displayed formula must be restricted to the relevant standard subclass.

component_coverage.gold_component: The universal nearest-neighbour representation claim fails because general vertically closed forms may contain arbitrary prolongation-coordinate differentials and need not have the prescribed mixed-shift pattern.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction states the special form, contrasts it with the arbitrary multi-index expansion, supplies a concrete nonconforming closed form, and proposes restricting the converse claim or using the general expansion.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify that the construction supports only that original solutions satisfy the resulting Euler–Lagrange equations, not equality of the original and Euler–Lagrange solution sets. ISSUE-002 explicitly states that the equivalent-Lagrangian wording overstates the conclusion and proposes the one-way formulation.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The argument establishes solution-set inclusion only; it does not establish the reverse implication required for an equivalent Lagrangian structure or equivalent systems.

component_coverage.gold_component: The claimed equivalence of the original multisymplectic system and the Euler–Lagrange system is unsupported; only one-way inclusion of original solutions is established.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction identifies the unsupported Lagrangian-existence and equivalence conclusion, explicitly notes that the resulting equations may be weaker, and requires weakening 'equivalent' or proving the missing result.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold issue concerns the domain of definition of a logarithmic Hamiltonian and its singular Euler–Lagrange term, requiring a positive second component. ISSUE-002 instead concerns unsupported vertical exactness and solution-set equivalence, with no diagnosis of the domain or logarithm restriction.
